findings.title: Whole-executor advance() results are never read when the block kernel is on
findings.problem: run_chain_case now also runs advance() on one executor that holds all head groups (whole_executor). Only check_advance_matches_step reads whole_checkpoint and whole_output, and it passes gdn_block_kernel::off. The three cases that pass when_available read only advanced_* and tally, and the whole-executor run takes no tally. So on an AMX host (AMX = the Intel tile-matrix instruction set) the block path for the second key head inside one executor runs with no assertion. The per-group run cannot cover it: with one key head per executor, key_head is 0, first_head is 0, and value_heads_per_group equals value_heads_per_key. A wrong offset or a wrong scalar_stride for key head 1 passes every test.
findings.evidence: Whole run, no tally: `executor.advance(order, first_position, block_kernel, gdn_token_rows{rows.mixed_qkv, rows.output_gate, rows.decay, rows.update, whole_output});` (lines 2757-2759). Only readers: `CHECK(result.whole_checkpoint == result.stepped_checkpoint); CHECK(same_floats(result.whole_output, result.stepped_output));` (lines 2790-2791, inside check_advance_matches_step, which calls `run_chain_case<geometry>(first_position, n_tokens, gdn_block_kernel::off)`). Code that only this run reaches with key_head = 1, gdn_rolling_executor.hpp lines 700-712: `size_t const first_head = key_head * value_heads_per_key;` `.value = working.window.value[0] + first_head * value_head_dim,` `.decay = working.window.decay[0] + first_head,` `.scalar_stride = value_heads_per_group,`.
findings.fix: In the cases that pass when_available ("stays close to step", "gives full windows ...", "gives a refused block ...") add `CHECK(result.whole_checkpoint == result.advanced_checkpoint);` and `CHECK(same_floats(result.whole_output, result.advanced_output));`. Both runs use the same windows and give the kernels the same inputs, so the bytes should be equal. Also pass a second tally to the whole-executor run and compare it with the per-group tally.

findings.title: Refused-block case: the output-row check cannot fail
findings.problem: The case puts +infinity into entry [key 0][column 0] of value head 1 and then compares the output rows of that head with those of step(). Every such row is all NaN on both sides, so the comparison holds whatever the fallback does. Hand computation: in token 0 the remembered value of column 0 is +inf or -inf, the correction has the opposite sign, and the new entry [0][0] is inf - inf = NaN. The raw output of column 0 is then NaN. postprocess() applies rmsnorm (RMS normalization over the 128 columns of the head), whose sum of squares is NaN, so all 128 outputs of the head are NaN for every token. The same holds if the fallback does not run at all: the block kernel's leftover output also has NaN in column 0 (its stage 1 product with the NaN pieces of the split infinity). All NaNs are the x86 default NaN 0xFFC00000, so memcmp is equal. Only the matrix comparison (`head_state(...)`, line 2938) can detect a missing or wrong fallback. It does so through columns 1 to 127, which stay finite.
findings.evidence: Test: `differing_rows += std::memcmp(result.advanced_output.data() + first, result.stepped_output.data() + first, geometry.value_head_dim * sizeof(float)) != 0;` ... `CHECK(differing_rows == 0);`. Executor postprocess (gdn_rolling_executor.hpp lines 809-812): `auto const normalized_head = rmsnorm(recurrent_head, operation.output_rms_norm_epsilon);`. expr.hpp line 888: `auto q = quadrance(x); auto ooss = 1.0f / sqrtf(q / expr_size<X> + epsilon); return ooss * std::forward<X>(x);`. Kernel (amx_gdn.cpp lines 226-229): `high = values & mask; remainder = values - high;` gives inf - inf = NaN for an infinite entry.
findings.fix: Keep the matrix comparison as the proof of the fallback and say so in the comment. Remove the row loop, or replace it by a check that can fail. A finite trigger does not help here: a correction of 2^100 or more makes the squares in rmsnorm overflow, and the rows become all zero. A useful replacement is the comparison of finding 1 (whole-executor bytes against per-group bytes), which covers the refused head in a second code path.

findings.title: Split case: the bound 2^-126 below 2^-103 is not a true bound (passes with seed 7 by a 2 % margin)
findings.problem: For a value with binary exponent -123 the kernel keeps only the first bf16 piece (the remainder is below 2^-130 and FTZ, the flush-to-zero bit of the MXCSR control register, makes it zero). If scale * high is below 2^-126 the output is flushed to zero, and the error is scale * value. That exceeds 2^-126 when the mantissa lies in (1.41421, 1.42188), which is 0.77 % of the mantissas (est. from the interval width). The largest possible error is 2^-126 * (1 + scale / 16) = 1.0055 * 2^-126. With std::mt19937 seed 7 the mantissa of that column (head 0, column 26) is 1.3846, so scale * value = 0.979 * 2^-126 and the check passes today. A changed seed, column order or draw count can make it fail without a kernel change. The comment "So the output may be off by 2^-126" states the same wrong bound.
findings.evidence: Test: `CHECK(std::fabs(static_cast<double>(output) - static_cast<double>(scale) * value) <= 0x1p-126);`. Kernel: `const __m512 remainder = _mm512_sub_ps(values, _mm512_castsi512_ps(high));` under `flush_subnormals_scope`, then `result[group] = _mm512_mul_ps(scaled_block_decay, ...)`. A Python model of split() with FTZ and DAZ on the 256 seed-7 values gave 210 exact values, 0 failures, and a worst error of 0.979 * 2^-126. The same model with mantissa 1.418 at exponent -123 gave output 0 and an error of 1.0027 * 2^-126.
findings.fix: Use a bound that holds for every mantissa, for example `<= 0x1.1p-126` (1.0625 * 2^-126), and correct the comment to "off by slightly more than 2^-126".

findings.title: Split case comment gives the wrong exponent range for head 1
findings.problem: The comment says head 1 covers exponents -22 to 105. exponent_of(1, 0) = 128 + 0 - 149 = -21. Exponent -22 belongs to head 0, column 127. Head 1 covers -21 to 105, and column 127 holds FLT_MAX.
findings.evidence: `// Head 0 covers exponents -149 .. -22, head 1 covers -22 .. 105 and 2^127.` next to `return static_cast<int>(head * VALUE_DIM_128 + column) - 149;`

findings.title: distinct_tally comment no longer matches the values after copy_cycles was removed

A leaf now has 14 tally keys. token_recurrence_cycles is key 10 but holds base + 11, and write_cycles is key 14 but holds base + 15. findings.evidence: `// A tally whose fields all differ: base + the position of the field's key in // a rendered leaf (items = base + 1, ..., write_cycles = base + 15).` followed by `t.pre_cycles = base + 9;` `t.recurrence_cycles[path_ix(gdn_path::token)] = base + 11;`

findings.title: gdn_stats.hpp header comment still names copy cycles and a 192-byte row
findings.problem: This file is outside the test lens, but the fix diff made two of its comment lines false. Line 48 still lists "copy" among the timed parts. Lines 87-88 state 192 bytes per row. worker_op_row now has 16 atomic 64-bit counters (128 bytes) and alignas(64), so its size is 128 bytes. Before the diff it had 17 counters (136 bytes, padded to 192). The example 2 x 56 x 24 x 192 = 516 KB is now 2 x 56 x 24 x 128 = 344 KB. No test checks the row size.
findings.evidence: Line 48: `//   the parts     start, pre, copy, recurrence (per path), post and write`. Lines 87-88: `// Memory when on: 2 classes x workers x operations x 192 bytes of rows, for // example 2 x 56 x 24 x 192 = 516 KB`. Struct at lines 212-227: items, head_tokens[3], amx_blocks, amx_fallback_blocks, chain_full_block_tokens, start_cycles, pre_cycles, recurrence_cycles[3], post_cycles, write_cycles, gdn_jobs, busy_cycles.

value.checked: Nothing was built or run; every prediction comes from reading the code at aacdd287c0, hand computation, and a small Python model of the split arithmetic. I found no assertion that will fail and no compile error in the seven cases: the gdn_token_rows{...} calls deduce (aggregate class template argument deduction, clang 19, C++23), the designated initializers of chain_case_result are in declaration order, block_kernel_available() is public, and the stats JSON strings match put_counts key by key. Hand results that agree with the tests: full_window_tokens matches advance() on all 16 (first_position, n_tokens) pairs (for example 7+128 gives [7,32), [32,64), [64,96), [96,128), [128,135) = 96 tokens in 3 full windows, 7+32 gives 0, 40+57 gives 32); the tally fields follow (amx head_tokens = 2 x amx tokens, amx_blocks = 4 per full window, chain_full_block_tokens = 0 when blocks run); the refused-block case gives 2 fallback blocks and 6 finished blocks on an AMX host and 0 and 0 without AMX; the non-finite-output case is refused only by the output rule and leaves the matrix unchanged; the MXCSR case can fail (no code sets FTZ or DAZ for the process); the split case gives 210 exact values with seed 7. One point is not proven by hand: `amx_fallback_blocks == 0` and `amx_blocks == 6` on an AMX host need the kernel to refuse no block for the test inputs (magnitudes below 1, refusal needs 2^100 or a non-finite value), and one run on an AMX host would confirm it; on a host without AMX the three numerics cases return after a WARN and the two executor cases check only the chain kernel.

verdicts.title: Whole-executor advance() results are never read when the block kernel is on
verdicts.reason:
The claim holds at the final head.
- The whole-executor run takes no tally: t/t_gated_delta_net.cpp:2757-2759 `executor.advance(order, first_position, block_kernel, gdn_token_rows{rows.mixed_qkv, rows.output_gate, rows.decay, rows.update, whole_output});`.
- Only check_advance_matches_step reads the whole-executor results (lines 2790-2791: `CHECK(result.whole_checkpoint == result.stepped_checkpoint); CHECK(same_floats(result.whole_output, result.stepped_output));`). It runs with `gdn_block_kernel::off` (line 2787).
- The three cases that pass when_available (lines 2840, 2893, 2932) read only advanced_*, stepped_* and tally. I read all three bodies.
- whole_executor is `gdn_rolling_executor<geometry, geometry.n_key_heads>` (line 2672). block_kernel_available() depends only on the head sizes, so on an AMX host this run does enter advance_window_with_block_kernel with key_head = 1. That is the only place where gdn_rolling_executor.hpp:700-712 runs with `first_head = key_head * value_heads_per_key` not zero and with `.scalar_stride = value_heads_per_group` different from value_heads_per_key. Nothing asserts on its result.
- Limit of the impact: production creates only the one-key-head executor (h/tron/models/gdn_execution.hpp:105 `using executor_type = gdn_rolling_head_executor<kernel_spec.geometry>;`). So the unchecked path is one that only this test instantiates. The gap is real, and its priority is low.
- The proposed checks are valid. pack_key_head and advance_value_head (src/tron/kernels/amx_gdn.cpp) read only the block addresses, the strides and the head's slices, and the scratch is written before it is read. So the per-group run and the whole run give the kernel the same inputs and must give the same bytes. One correction to the second part of the fix is below.
verdicts.corrected_fix: In the three when_available cases add `CHECK(result.whole_checkpoint == result.advanced_checkpoint);` and `CHECK(same_floats(result.whole_output, result.advanced_output));`. If a second tally is passed to the whole-executor run, compare only the count fields (head_tokens, amx_blocks, amx_fallback_blocks, chain_full_block_tokens). The *_cycles fields are time stamp differences and differ between two runs.

verdicts.title: Refused-block case: the output-row check cannot fail
verdicts.reason:
I walked both paths and the rows are all NaN on both sides.
- The test writes +infinity at [value head 1][key 0][column 0] (t/t_gated_delta_net.cpp:2701).
- step() path, gdn_recurrence in h/tron/kernels/gated_delta_net.hpp: the remembered value of column 0 is +inf or -inf, and delta has the opposite sign. `fp32s const new_state = fma(normalized_key, delta[chunk], state[value_head][key_coordinate].chunk(chunk) * decay_values);` is then inf - inf = NaN at [0][0]. `result[chunk] = fma(scaled_query, new_state, result[chunk]);` makes output column 0 NaN.
- postprocess (gdn_rolling_executor.hpp:809-812) calls rmsnorm. h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp:888-891: `auto q = quadrance(x); auto ooss = 1.0f / sqrtf(q / expr_size<X> + epsilon); return ooss * std::forward<X>(x);`. A NaN sum of squares makes all 128 columns NaN. The NaN stays in the matrix, so this holds for every token.
- Missing-fallback path: the kernel stores every output before it tests for refusal. src/tron/kernels/amx_gdn.cpp:477 `_mm512_store_ps(token_output + group * LANES_16, out);` is inside the token loop, and `return false;` is at line 489 after the loop. Stage 1 reads the infinity through split() (line 227: `const __m512 remainder = _mm512_sub_ps(values, _mm512_castsi512_ps(high));` = inf - inf = NaN). So column 0 of every stage 1 product is NaN, and so is column 0 of every leftover output. rmsnorm then makes those rows all NaN too.
- Every NaN here comes from an invalid operation or from propagating one, so all carry the x86 default NaN bits and memcmp is equal.
- So the loop at lines 2941-2948 passes with or without the fallback. The matrix comparison at lines 2938-2939 does have power: on refusal the kernel leaves the matrix untouched (stage 4 comes after `return false`), and columns 1 to 127 stay finite and must change over 64 tokens.
- Two small corrections to the finding's text. (1) With a finite trigger the rows become signed zeros (ooss = 0 times a finite value), so the comparison would test only signs. The conclusion that a finite trigger does not help still holds. (2) The suggested replacement by the output rows of the whole-executor run is equally vacuous for this head: those rows are all NaN as well. Only the checkpoint comparison of that run adds coverage.
verdicts.corrected_fix: Remove the row loop (lines 2940-2948) and say in the case comment that the matrix comparison is the proof of the fallback. To cover the fallback in the second code path, add `CHECK(head_state(result.whole_checkpoint) == head_state(result.stepped_checkpoint));` (or `CHECK(result.whole_checkpoint == result.advanced_checkpoint);`). Do not add an output-row comparison for the infinite head as coverage: its rows are NaN in every run.

verdicts.title: Split case: the bound 2^-126 below 2^-103 is not a true bound (passes with seed 7 by a 2 % margin)
verdicts.reason:
The analysis is right, and the case passes today. Severity nit is correct.
- Kernel behaviour for a value with binary exponent -123: the first bf16 piece holds bits down to 2^-130, so the remainder (`_mm512_sub_ps(values, high)`, amx_gdn.cpp:227) is below 2^-130. It is subnormal. The kernel runs under `flush_subnormals_scope` (line 340), and the tile product also reads a subnormal bf16 as zero. Only the first piece is kept.
- The output is `_mm512_mul_ps(scaled_block_decay, ...)` (line 453) = scale * high with flush-to-zero. scale as FP32 is 0.0883883461. When scale * high is below 2^-126 the output is 0 and the error is scale * value.
- scale * value exceeds 2^-126 when the mantissa is above 1.4142136. The first piece stays at mantissa 1.4140625 (scale * high = 0.99989 * 2^-126, still flushed) until mantissa 1.421875. So mantissas in (1.4142136, 1.421875) fail the check `<= 0x1p-126` (t/t_amx_gdn_numerics.cpp:504-505). That is 0.77 % of the mantissa range. The largest error is 1.0054 * 2^-126.
- No other exponent can exceed 2^-126: at -124 and below scale * value is under 0.71 * 2^-126, and at -122 and above scale * high is a normal number and the lost part is under 0.09 * 2^-126.
- Seed check, computed with my own model of std::mt19937(7) and the libstdc++ distributions (one draw for the coin, one for the mantissa): head 0, column 26 (exponent -123) has mantissa 1.384650. scale * value = 0.9791 * 2^-126, so the check passes with a 2.1 % margin. This matches the finding. It depends on the draw order of the standard library.
- The comment at lines 445-446 ("So the output may be off by 2^-126") states the same bound.
- The proposed bound 0x1.1p-126 (1.0625 * 2^-126) is above the largest error, so the fix is valid.

verdicts.title: Split case comment gives the wrong exponent range for head 1
verdicts.reason: t/t_amx_gdn_numerics.cpp:458 says `// Head 0 covers exponents -149 .. -22, head 1 covers -22 .. 105 and 2^127.` The lambda below it returns `static_cast<int>(head * VALUE_DIM_128 + column) - 149`. So exponent_of(0, 127) = -22 and exponent_of(1, 0) = -21. Head 1 covers -21 to 105 in columns 0 to 126, and column 127 is replaced by `sign * std::numeric_limits<float>::max()`. The comment is off by one for head 1. It is a comment-only defect in a test that the fix diff added. No check depends on it.
